slack.reconnect: Reconnect verifies or replaces credentials for this same Slack app. It does not reinstall the app or change its workspace or channel membership.
slack.remove: Myrmidon archives the endpoint, stops new ingress, and retires its saved Slack credentials. It does not uninstall the Slack app: the app remains installed, and its bot remains in channels, until you remove them in Slack.

github.reconnect: Reconnect verifies this same App and installation, then updates its webhook URL, secret, and secure delivery settings. It does not reinstall the App or change repository access.
github.remove: Myrmidon archives the endpoint, stops new ingress, and retires its saved App key and webhook secret. It does not uninstall the GitHub App: the App, its installations, and its webhook settings remain until you remove or update them on GitHub.

discord.reconnect: Reconnect verifies this same Discord application and server installation. It does not add or remove the bot from the server.
discord.remove: Myrmidon archives the endpoint, stops its Myrmidon Gateway connection, and retires its saved bot token. It does not uninstall the bot: the bot remains in the Discord server, and the application remains in the Developer Portal, until you remove them there.

teams.reconnect: Reconnect verifies this same Microsoft app, tenant, and bot identity. It does not upload or reinstall the Teams app.
teams.remove: Myrmidon archives the endpoint, stops new ingress, and retires its saved client secret. It does not uninstall the Teams app: the Entra app registration, Azure Bot, custom Teams app, and Teams installations remain until you remove them in Microsoft.

photon.reconnect: Reconnect verifies the same Photon project and line allocation, then recovers eligible missed messages.
photon.remove: Disconnect archives this channel and removes its saved secret. Your Photon project, number, subscription, and Messages history remain in Photon.

telegram.reconnect: Reconnect verifies this same BotFather bot and automatically refreshes its Myrmidon webhook and command menu.
telegram.remove: Myrmidon archives the endpoint and queues durable removal of its Telegram webhook and command menu. After Telegram confirms that cleanup, Myrmidon retires the saved token. The BotFather bot and its chat memberships remain until you remove them in Telegram.

resolution.fileInfoUnknown: The file upload was confirmed, but its Teams notification was not. Check Teams first. Retrying sends only that notification, not the file bytes, and may create a duplicate card.

resolution.uploadUnknown: The file may already exist in OneDrive. Cancelling stops this Myrmidon transfer; it does not delete remote bytes. Uploads cannot be marked delivered or retried from this uncertain state.
resolution.default: Myrmidon lost confirmation after sending. Check the provider conversation first. Retrying can create a duplicate message.

github.descriptionNew: Configure its webhook and permissions, then verify the App with Myrmidon.
github.step1: Under the target user or organization, create a new GitHub App. Give it a globally unique name (34 characters or fewer), use the Myrmidon homepage URL below, and leave user authorization off.

github.step3: Under Repository permissions, set <0>Issues</0> and <0>Pull requests</0> to <0>Read & write</0>. Leave every other permission at its default; Metadata remains read-only.
github.step4: Subscribe to <0>Issue comment</0> (<1>issue_comment</1>), <0>Pull request review comment</0> (<1>pull_request_review_comment</1>). GitHub sends <1>installation</1> and <1>installation_repositories</1> to every GitHub App automatically; they are not selectable here.
github.step5: Choose <0>Only on this account</0>, create the App, copy its App ID, generate one private key, then install it on the selected repositories.

teams.title: Connect {{agent}} to Microsoft Teams
teams.descriptionRepair: Reconnect verifies this same Microsoft app, tenant, and bot identity. It does not upload or reinstall the Teams app. Leave fields blank to reuse saved credentials.
teams.descriptionNew: Use your own Microsoft app credentials for this bot.
teams.requirements: This setup requires a Microsoft 365 work or school organization where you can register an Entra app, create an Azure Bot, and upload or install a Teams app. Personal or free Teams accounts at teams.live.com cannot complete this setup. This release supports Microsoft 365 commercial cloud tenants only; GCC, GCC High, DoD, and Microsoft 365 operated by 21Vianet are not supported yet.
teams.step1: In Microsoft Entra, create a single-tenant app registration. Copy its Application (client) ID and Directory (tenant) ID, then create a client secret and copy its value.
teams.step2: In Azure, create an Azure Bot. Choose Single Tenant, use that Application ID, set its messaging endpoint to the Myrmidon URL below, and add the Microsoft Teams channel.
teams.step3: In Teams Developer Portal, create an app, add a bot with the same Application ID, then apply the manifest settings shown below. The block binds the Teams resource-specific consent permissions to that Entra app; these are not Microsoft Graph permissions in Entra. These permissions let the installed app receive every message in a team or group chat without an @mention, so describe that access to installers. Download the package and install it in the target team or group chat.
teams.fieldMapIntro: Use these exact portal sections and reuse the same Application ID in all three places.
teams.fieldMap1: <0>Microsoft Entra admin center · App registrations</0>: select <0>New registration</0>, choose <0>Accounts in this organizational directory only (Single tenant)</0>, then select <0>Register</0>. Copy <0>Application (client) ID</0> and <0>Directory (tenant) ID</0>. Under <0>Certificates & secrets · Client secrets</0>, select <0>New client secret</0> and copy its <0>Value</0>, not its Secret ID.
teams.fieldMap2: <0>Azure · Create Azure Bot</0>: set <0>Microsoft App ID</0> to <0>Single Tenant</0>, set <0>Creation type</0> to <0>Use existing app registration</0>, and enter the Application ID and Tenant ID above. After creation, open <0>Settings · Configuration</0> and paste the Myrmidon <0>Messaging endpoint</0>; then open <0>Settings · Channels</0> and enable <0>Microsoft Teams</0>.
teams.fieldMap3: <0>Teams Developer Portal · Apps</0>: select <0>New app</0>. Under <0>Configure · App features · Bot</0>, add an existing bot using the same Application ID; enable <0>Personal</0>, <0>Team</0>, and <0>Group chat</0> scopes plus file support. Under <0>Configure · Permissions</0>, add the two RSC <0>Application</0> permissions shown below. Complete the required app details and icons, explain that the app can receive every message in an installed team or group chat, then download the app package.
teams.fieldMap4: <0>Microsoft Teams · Apps · Manage your apps</0>: select <0>Upload an app · Upload a custom app</0>, choose the downloaded package, and install it in each intended personal chat, group chat, or team. One team install covers its standard channels. Private and shared channels require a separate app installation and are not supported by this release. If upload is unavailable, a Teams administrator must enable or approve custom apps.
teams.manifestNote: Enter the Application / Client ID above before copying so the block contains the real bot identity. This block contains the Myrmidon-specific fields to verify in Developer Portal or merge into a complete Teams app manifest. It is not a complete app package; Developer Portal supplies the remaining required metadata and packages the manifest with your app icons.
teams.ssoNote: Myrmidon does not use Teams single sign-on in this release. The copied <1>webApplicationInfo</1> entry only associates the RSC permissions with the same Entra Application ID. Its nonempty resource is an RSC placeholder; you do not need to register an Entra Application ID URI or add delegated Microsoft Graph permissions.
teams.rscNote: The two application RSC permissions let the bot receive every message, without an @mention, in each team or group chat where it is installed. Myrmidon retains and acts only on messages admitted by your Myrmidon reach and access rules. Make this provider access clear in the app description shown to installers.
teams.scopeNote: This release supports personal chats, group chats, and standard team channels—not private channels. <1>supportsFiles: true</1> enables native file receipt and consent-based sending in personal chats; channel and group-chat files need a separate Microsoft Graph connection and are not ingested here.

slackFinish.title: Finish Slack setup
slackFinish.description: Point the Slack app at Myrmidon now that its signing secret is connected.
slackFinish.commandHelp: Start work with <1>{{command}} investigate this</1>. In a direct message, use <1>{{command}} status</1>, <1>{{command}} new</1>, or <1>{{command}} close</1>. Slack's bare <1>/status</1> command is not a Myrmidon control.
slackFinish.step1: Return to <0>App Manifest</0> in Slack and click <0>Save Changes</0>. The copied manifest already contains the event, interaction, and slash-command URLs. Slack verifies the Events URL when you save; Myrmidon records Interactivity and slash command health only after each signed callback is observed.

slack.step2: Open <0>OAuth & Permissions</0>, install the app to the workspace, and copy its Bot User OAuth Token.
slack.step3: Open <0>Basic Information</0> and copy its Signing Secret.

guidance.telegramGuestOn: Tap Start in Telegram to discover your account. Until linked, it is a restricted guest and still needs a sandbox-backed isolated run; test that path intentionally, or link it in Access and then send the test message.
guidance.guestOn: Until linked, the account is a restricted guest and still needs a sandbox-backed isolated run. Test that guest path intentionally, or link the account in Access and then {{action}}.
guidance.unlinkedGuestOff: An observed external account is unlinked, and isolated guest work is off, so it cannot safely start {{agent}}. Link the account in Access, then {{action}}; Myrmidon does not replay the refused request.
guidance.unlinkedGuestOn: An unlinked account is a restricted guest and still needs a sandbox-backed isolated run. Test guest access intentionally, or link the account in Access and then {{action}}.
